subject: Unit-cost validation and MAP action items: traffic & caching assumptions

Subject: Unit-cost validation for MAP

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move into a MAP + evaluation window, the procurement and engineering teams want a clear checklist for the unit-economics checks we need to complete before we sign the SOW. I attached a small sample of our usage (Brightline_USAGE_sample.csv) — high level profile: 12k unique monthly users, a heavy tail of conversational history (~60% of calls include a 1.5–2k token context), and spikes during morning hours.

Key asks from our side:
- A short list of assumptions you need to validate tokens/$ for our MAP (batching, KV/prefix caching expectations, quantization profile suggested)
- An estimate for expected median and p95 token cost under our traffic profile (order of magnitude is fine)
- Any workload changes that would materially change the cost (e.g., prefetching, extended context, multi-turn reranking)
- Proposed timeline for a small eval we can run that proves your unit-costs (sample dataset + 1 week run)

We have a procurement gating review on Dec 10, so if possible we’d like a short draft MAP checklist and timeline by end of week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if a synchronous check is easier.

— Elena
Elena Ramos
Sr. Director, Product
Brightline Health

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the usage sample, that helps a lot. I sketched a compact checklist below that we can turn into a MAP appendix. I also uploaded an initial spreadsheet with a conservative tokens/$ sketch (mk_unitcost_checker.xlsx) and a draft MAP timeline in the Drive link.

Proposal: quick checklist for MAP unit-econ validation (what we will deliver in the evaluation window)
1) Traffic & token profile validation
   - We’ll ingest the sample and produce per-call token distributions (median, mean, p50/p75/p95)
   - Flag any multi-turn conversations that push >4k context tokens (these are outliers for our standard configs)
2) Batching & latency constraints
   - Run 3 workload shapes: steady-state baseline, morning spike sim, and 3-minute burst spike
   - For each shape, measure median/p95 latency at 1) small batch (1–4 reqs), 2) medium batch (8–16), and 3) large (32+) — to show cost/latency tradeoffs
3) Caching / prefix reuse assumptions
   - Verify expected prefix reuse fraction from sample (we’ll estimate % cache hits on KV cache for 1-week sim)
   - Provide suggestions for prefix-keying heuristics (session id vs user id vs conversation fingerprint)
4) Quantization profile & model variant recommendations
   - For Brightline profile we recommend testing (a) fp16 baseline, (b) 4-bit quantized variant with recommended prompt-tuning, (c) CPU fallback for low-throughput tails
5) Cost per 1M tokens scenarios
   - Produce three scenarios (conservative / expected / optimistic) and map to tokens/$ and per-user monthly spend
6) Acceptance criteria for MAP
   - Difference between expected and observed median tokens/$ <= 20% on the eval run
   - p95 latency under 600ms (or agreed SLO) with batched config for peak profile

Timeline (draft):
- Tue (12/1): quick data ingest and token-distribution report (this week)
- Wed–Thu (12/2–12/3): run batch/cache sensitivity sims (48h)
- Fri (12/4): share initial tokens/$ scenarios and config recommendations
- Mon (12/7): 1-hour alignment call to lock MAP appendix and acceptance gates
- Wed (12/9): final MAP doc for procurement review (Dec 10)

Action items for Brightline (short):
- Confirm whether session history retention includes attachments and images (those change tokens significantly)
- Provide a 48-hour sample of peak-hour traffic if possible (we can work with the CSV you sent)

We can trim table granularity if procurement wants a one-page summary. If that timeline looks good I’ll assign the eval sprint and Priya will touch the procurement gating items.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference
